initial_candidates.title: VaR limit breach on MOCK_PTF_ATLAS MOCK_PC_FLOW with 3 consecutive days above hard bound
initial_candidates.claim: MOCK_LIMIT_01_01 (VaR, MEUR, upper bound 7.0) was breached on 2026-03-25, 2026-03-26, and 2026-03-27, with worst value 7.55 on 2026-03-26 (utilization 107.86%). This is a hard-bound breach population of 3 observations, confirmed by deterministic analysis.
analysis_performed: Identified breach observations from deterministic limit consumption analysis.
Verified worst value and utilization from the flagged candidate.
alternative_explanations: Market move or new activity could explain the spike.
Limit may have been temporarily increased but not reflected in the series.
initial_candidates.recommendation: Review the cause of the breach and confirm whether the limit increase was approved before the breach dates.

initial_candidates.title: Limit increase effective before workflow approval after VaR breach on MOCK_PC_FLOW
initial_candidates.claim: MOCK_LIMIT_01_01 upper bound changed from 7.0 to 9.0 effective 2026-04-01, but the associated Colibris workflow (excess 880001) has request date 2026-04-02, trader approval 2026-04-12, and risk approval 2026-04-15. The effective date precedes the recorded approvals, and the change follows a 3-day breach in late March 2026. This is a material governance candidate.
analysis_performed: Compared effective date from SGMR with workflow milestones from Colibris.
Noted prior breach observations from deterministic analysis.
alternative_explanations: Effective date may be backdated for legitimate reasons.
Workflow dates may be system processing dates, not approval dates.
initial_candidates.recommendation: Obtain the limit change approval and effective-date history to confirm whether the change was retrospective.

initial_candidates.title: Recurring excess events on MOCK_PC_FLOW VaR with 9 events and 2 still open
initial_candidates.claim: MOCK_PC_FLOW VaR (limit 7.0 MEUR) had 9 excess events between 2025-07-01 and 2026-04-07, with 2 still open as of 2026-06-30. Max recorded usage reached 121.67%. This indicates a recurring pattern of limit breaches on this perimeter.
analysis_performed: Counted excess events per PC/metric from deterministic workflow analysis.
Identified open events and max usage.
alternative_explanations: Recurrence may reflect normal market-making activity in a volatile period.
Some events may be duplicates or system artifacts.
initial_candidates.recommendation: Investigate the root cause of repeated breaches and consider whether the limit level is appropriate.

initial_candidates.title: Open excess events past recorded deadlines on multiple perimeters
initial_candidates.claim: Seven excess events remain open as of 2026-06-30, and at least six of them have both explanation action deadlines and technical deadlines in the past (e.g., excess 590000 created 2025-07-01 with deadlines 2025-07-08 and 2025-07-15). This suggests unresolved or stale control items.
analysis_performed: Identified open excess events with past deadlines from deterministic workflow analysis.
Confirmed open state and deadline dates.
alternative_explanations: Extract may be stale; events may have been closed after the as-of date.
Deadlines may be system-generated and not contractual SLAs.
initial_candidates.recommendation: Confirm extract freshness and obtain closure evidence for these open events.

initial_candidates.title: Limit increase status APPROVED without increase ID on multiple excess records
initial_candidates.claim: At least 10 excess records have increaseWorkflowStatus 'APPROVED' but increaseId equals 0 (e.g., excess 590000, 590005, 590010). This is an internal consistency issue in the Colibris data.
analysis_performed: Scanned excess records for increase status without ID from deterministic workflow analysis.
alternative_explanations: Increase ID may be populated in a separate system not included.
Status may be inherited from a parent limit.
initial_candidates.recommendation: Verify the increase workflow data completeness and correct the mapping.

initial_candidates.title: Workflow date order mismatch on excess 880001 and 880002
initial_candidates.claim: Excess records 880001 and 880002 have explanation and validation timestamps before the excess creation date, indicating a date order mismatch in the workflow data.
analysis_performed: Identified date order mismatches from deterministic workflow analysis.
alternative_explanations: Creation date may be a system processing date, not the event date.
Timestamps may be in different timezones.
initial_candidates.recommendation: Investigate the timestamp semantics and correct the data.

initial_candidates.title: Cross-source limit type mismatch between Colibris and SGMR for VaR limits
initial_candidates.claim: Colibris records for MOCK_PC_FLOW and MOCK_PC_HEDGE VaR excesses show limitType 'RELATIVE_THRESHOLD', while the matched SGMR limit definitions are 'ABSOLUTE_THRESHOLD'. This discrepancy affects the interpretation of the limit type and requires confirmation.
analysis_performed: Compared limit types across sources from deterministic cross-source consistency analysis.
alternative_explanations: Colibris may describe the event trigger type, not the limit type.
Different systems may use different terminology.
initial_candidates.recommendation: Clarify the meaning of limitType in each system and align definitions.

initial_candidates.title: Event-to-SGMR row reconciliation unresolved due to missing unique bridge
initial_candidates.claim: Only 25 of 50 Colibris events have semantic date matches with SGMR rows, and no unique direct ID matches exist. The event-to-observation reconciliation is UNRESOLVED because a unique source-backed sgmrId bridge is required.
analysis_performed: Reviewed cross-source consistency results showing unresolved reconciliation.
alternative_explanations: Semantic matching may be ambiguous because one PC maps to multiple portfolios.
Weekend/holiday dates may legitimately lack SGMR rows.
initial_candidates.recommendation: Obtain a documented unique ID bridge between Colibris and SGMR to enable event-level reconciliation.
